claim: Theta bursts in i/vHP had significantly higher occurrence (8.1 ± 0.2 oscillations/min, n = 103 mice) compared to dHP (5.2 ± 0.3 oscillations/min, n = 41 mice; p<0.001).

claim: Theta bursts in i/vHP had larger amplitude (110.6 ± 5.6 µV) compared to dHP (92.9 ± 2.6 µV; p=0.015).
source: The theta bursts in i/vHP had significantly higher occurrence (i/vHP: 8.1 ± 0.2 oscillations/min, n = 103 mice vs. dHP: 5.2 ± 0.3 oscillations/min, n = 41 mice; p<0.001), larger amplitude (i/vHP:110.6 ± 5.6 µV vs. dHP: 92.9 ± 2.6 µV; p=0.015)

claim: Theta bursts in i/vHP had shorter duration (3.5 ± 0.1 s) compared to dHP (4.3 ± 0.1 s, p<0.001).

evidence: Temporal measurements of theta burst events showing statistically significant differences in duration.

claim: Theta band power was significantly stronger in dHP (relative power: 13.0 ± 1.3, n = 41 mice) compared to i/vHP (10.3 ± 0.5, n = 103 mice; p=0.026).

claim: Beta frequency power (12–30 Hz) was similar between dHP (15.0 ± 1.6) and i/vHP (13.2 ± 0.7, p=0.22).

evidence: Power spectral analysis showing no statistically significant difference in beta band power.

claim: Gamma frequency power (30–100 Hz) was similar between dHP (6.3 ± 0.6) and i/vHP (5.2 ± 0.3, p=0.073).
evidence: Power spectral analysis showing no statistically significant difference in gamma band power.

source: Blue light stimulation (473 nm) confined to i/vHP of Dlx5/6–ChETA mice (n = 19) led to a significant reduction of hippocampal power in all frequency bands (theta: p=0.024, beta: p=0.018, gamma: p=0.044).

source: Taking into account that viral transduction, which usually requires 10–14 days for stable expression, is only of limited usability to investigate local network interactions during development, IUE seems to represent the method of choice for manipulating circuits at this early age.
evidence: Statement about methodological limitations based on established knowledge.

claim: IUE enables targeting of precursor cells of neuronal and glial subpopulations, based on their distinct spatial and temporal patterns of generation in the ventricular zone.
source: IUE enables targeting of precursor cells of neuronal and glial subpopulations, based on their distinct spatial and temporal patterns of generation in the ventricular zone (Tabata and Nakajima, 2001; Borrell et al., 2005; Niwa et al., 2010; Hoerder-Suabedissen and Molnár, 2015).
evidence: Statement about methodological capabilities supported by citations.

claim: IUE based on two electrode paddles enabled selective targeting of pyramidal neurons in the CA1 area of dHP in more than half of the pups per litter.
source: IUE based on two electrode paddles enabled selective targeting of pyramidal neurons in the CA1 area of dHP in more than half of the pups per litter (Figure 5—figure supplement 1)
evidence: Statement about methodological success rate with reference to supplementary figure.

claim: Two-electrode IUE completely failed (0 out of 32 mice) to target pyramidal neurons in i/vHP.
source: but it completely failed (0 out of 32 mice) to target these neurons in i/vHP.
evidence: Statement about methodological limitation based on experimental results.

claim: The modified IUE protocol based on three electrodes allows reliable transfection at brain locations that are only able to be sporadically targeted by two electrodes.
source: This protocol, although more complicated and time consuming, allows reliable transfection at brain locations that are only able to be sporadically targeted by two electrodes
evidence: Statement about methodological improvement based on experimental results.

claim: Abundant literature links theta frequency coupling within prefrontal-hippocampal networks to cognitive performance and emotional states of adults.
source: Abundant literature links theta frequency coupling within prefrontal-hippocampal networks to cognitive performance and emotional states of adults (Adhikari et al., 2010; Xu and Südhof, 2013; Spellman et al., 2015; Hallock et al., 2016; Place et al., 2016; Ye et al., 2017).
evidence: Statement about established knowledge supported by multiple citations.

claim: The maturation of cognitive abilities is a process even more protracted than sensory development and starts during second-third postnatal week.
source: The maturation of cognitive abilities is a process even more protracted than sensory development and starts during second-third postnatal week (Hanganu-Opatz, 2010; Cirelli and Tononi, 2015).
evidence: Statement about developmental timeline supported by citations.

claim: Recognition memory can be easily monitored at early age and seems to critically rely on structurally and functionally intact prefrontal-hippocampal networks.
source: Some of these abilities, such as recognition memory, can be easily monitored at early age and seems to critically rely on structurally and functionally intact prefrontal-hippocampal networks (Krüger et al., 2012).
evidence: Statement about behavioral capabilities and their neural substrates supported by citation.

claim: Following the general rules of activity-dependent plasticity, the precisely timed excitatory inputs from the i/vHP to the PL might facilitate the wiring of local prefrontal circuitry and enable the refinement of behaviorally relevant communication scaffold between the two regions.
source: Following the general rules of activity-dependent plasticity (Hubel et al., 1977; Huberman et al., 2006; Xu et al., 2011; Yasuda et al., 2011), the precisely timed excitatory inputs from the i/vHP to the PL might facilitate the wiring of local prefrontal circuitry and enable the refinement of behaviorally relevant communication scaffold between the two regions.
evidence: Proposed mechanism based on established principles of neural development supported by citations.

claim: The prefrontal activity driven by projection neurons in the HP acts as a template, having a pre-adaptive function that facilitates the tuning of circuits with regard to future conditions.
source: By these means, the prefrontal activity driven by projection neurons in the HP act as a template, having a pre-adaptive function that facilitates the tuning of circuits with regard to future conditions.
evidence: Proposed functional role based on inference from experimental findings.

claim: The dHP, which receives dense projections from the entorhinal cortex, is mainly involved in spatial navigation in adults.
source: For example, the dHP, which receives dense projections from the entorhinal cortex (Witter and Amaral, 2004), is mainly involved in spatial navigation (O'Keefe and Nadel, 1978; Moser et al., 1995; Moser et al., 1998).
evidence: Statement about functional specialization in adults supported by citations.

claim: The ventral part of HP receives strong cholinergic and dopaminergic innervation and contributes to processing of non-spatial information.
source: In contrast, the ventral part receives strong cholinergic and dopaminergic innervation (Witter et al., 1989; Pitkänen et al., 2000) and contributes to processing of non-spatial information (Bannerman et al., 2003; Bast et al., 2009).
evidence: Statement about anatomical connectivity and functional specialization supported by citations.

claim: The direct unilateral projections from hippocampal CA1 area to PL have been extensively investigated in adult brain and are present already at neonatal age.
source: The direct unilateral projections from hippocampal CA1 area to PL have been extensively investigated in adult brain (Swanson, 1981; Jay and Witter, 1991; Vertes et al., 2007) and are present already at neonatal age (Brockmann et al., 2011; Hartung et al., 2016).
evidence: Statement about anatomical connectivity supported by citations to both adult and developmental studies.

claim: The used light power did not cause local tissue heating that might interfere with neuronal spiking.
source: Our previous experimental data and modeling work showed that the used light power did not cause local tissue heating that might interfere with neuronal spiking (Stujenske et al., 2015; Bitzenhofer et al., 2017b).
evidence: Statement about control for potential confound supported by citations to previous work.

claim: For stimulation frequencies >16 Hz, the firing lost the precise timing by light, most likely due to the immaturity of neurons and their projections.
source: For stimulation frequencies >16 Hz, the firing lost the precise timing by light, most likely due to the immaturity of neurons and their projections.
evidence: Observation from optogenetic experiments with proposed explanation based on developmental considerations.

claim: Rhythmic firing of prelimbic neurons was not detected after light activation of hippocampal subdivisions, most likely because hippocampal axons were rather sparse.
source: Rhythmic firing of prelimbic neurons was not detected after light activation of hippocampal subdivisions, most likely because hippocampal axons were rather sparse.
evidence: Observation from optogenetic experiments with proposed explanation based on anatomical considerations.

claim: Already at neonatal age, prefrontal oscillations are generated shortly (~100 ms) after hippocampal SPWs-ripples.
source: Simultaneous recordings from neonatal CA1 area either in dHP or i/vHP and PL showed that already at neonatal age, prefrontal oscillations are generated shortly (~100 ms) after hippocampal SPWs-ripples.
evidence: Temporal analysis of simultaneous recordings showing time-locked relationship.

claim: The level of coherence between PL and HP is a genuine feature of investigated neonatal networks and not the result of non-specific and conduction synchrony, since only the imaginary component of the coherence spectrum was considered, which excludes zero time-lag synchronization.
source: In line with previous investigations, this level of coherence is a genuine feature of investigated neonatal networks and not the result of non-specific and conduction synchrony, since we considered only the imaginary component of the coherence spectrum, which excludes zero time-lag synchronization (Nolte et al., 2004).
evidence: Methodological consideration to exclude confounds, supported by citation.

claim: The investigation focused on PL, since in adults it is the prefrontal subdivision with the most dense innervation from HP.
source: The entire investigation focused on PL, since in adults it is the prefrontal subdivision with the most dense innervation from HP (Jay and Witter, 1991; Vertes et al., 2007).
evidence: Justification for experimental design based on anatomical knowledge from adult studies.
